title: Source tax: residence abroad and cross-border questions
purpose: Ask Liechtenstein and Germany residents the cross-border questions (their expectation for the year). Decide whether there is in principle no liability (Liechtenstein, flagged for HR), or whether the cross-border or the normal tariff applies.

stories.title: Derive the calculator's residence answers from the home address and ask cross-border questions only of Germany and Liechtenstein residents
stories.i_want: Lonio to take my country of residence from my home address and to ask me cross-border questions only if I live in Germany or Liechtenstein
stories.so_that: I give my country of residence only once and am not asked questions that no receiving party needs for me, while the source tax side still gets the residence answers the Zurich calculator needs
stories.priority_reason: Avoids double questions and unneeded data (G-01, G-08); the cross-border results themselves are covered by the Germany and Liechtenstein stories.

acceptance_criteria.title: Residence for source tax is not asked separately
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has entered the country of their home address that applies on the first working day (assumption to be verified by a domain expert, D-041)
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio determines the calculator's residence answers
acceptance_criteria.then: the calculator's 'main residence in Switzerland' and 'country of residence' answers (Germany, Liechtenstein or other country) are taken from that country; the employee is not asked a separate residence question

acceptance_criteria.title: No cross-border questions outside Germany and Liechtenstein
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Switzerland or in a country other than Germany or Liechtenstein
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee goes through the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: none of the questions on daily return, certificate of residence, reasonableness of daily return or non-return days is asked; an employee living in another country is subject to source tax and gets the normal (not the cross-border) tariff

stories.title: Germany: daily return and certificate of residence
stories.i_want: every employee living in Germany to state whether they expect to return daily to their main residence in Germany and, if so, whether they have a certificate of residence
stories.so_that: Lonio can decide, as the Zurich calculator does, whether the cross-border tariff or the normal tariff applies and compute the correct tariff code
stories.priority_reason: Lonio now computes the tariff code instead of HR (D-001); without these answers the tariff for Germany residents is wrong, and HR finds the cross-border cases the most complicated (F-hr_transcript-8595fb).

acceptance_criteria.title: Daily return to Germany is asked of every Germany resident
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's home address on the first working day is in Germany (so they are subject to source tax whatever their nationality)
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches the source tax questions
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked whether they expect to return daily to their main residence in Germany, answered 'yes' or 'no'; the answer is required; it is not asked of anyone living elsewhere. The answer is used for the source tax tariff code and recorded for HR

acceptance_criteria.title: Certificate of residence is asked only with daily return
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee answers the daily return question
acceptance_criteria.then: only with 'yes' is the employee asked whether they have a certificate of residence, answered 'yes', 'no' or 'not yet'; the answer is required when asked. 'not yet' is a valid answer for a new hire. The certificate itself is handed to HR outside Lonio; Lonio offers no upload

acceptance_criteria.title: Daily return with certificate gives the cross-border tariff
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Germany and expects to return daily
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio decides between cross-border and normal tariff
acceptance_criteria.then: with a certificate of residence ('yes') the cross-border tariff applies (A becomes L, B becomes M, C becomes N, H becomes P); with 'no' or 'not yet' the normal tariff applies. The result is always derived again from the latest answers. Cross-border results for tariffs A, B and H were only spot-checked in the calculator and are part of the go-live comparison (see OQ-calculator-coverage)

stories.title: Germany: no daily return - reasonableness and more than 60 non-return days
stories.i_want: an employee living in Germany who does not expect to return daily to state whether daily return would basically be reasonable (less than 100 km driving distance) and, if so, whether they expect more than 60 work-related non-return days in the calendar year
stories.so_that: Lonio can decide, as the Zurich calculator does, whether the cross-border tariff or the normal tariff applies
stories.priority_reason: Lonio computes the tariff code itself (D-001); a missing or wrong answer leads to a wrong tariff for Germany residents.

acceptance_criteria.title: Reasonableness of daily return is asked without daily return
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Germany and answered that they do not expect to return daily
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee continues with the source tax questions
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked whether daily return would basically be reasonable (less than 100 km driving distance), answered 'yes' or 'no'; the answer is required; it is not asked of employees who return daily or live elsewhere. The answer is used for the tariff code and recorded for HR

acceptance_criteria.title: More than 60 non-return days is asked only when daily return is reasonable
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Germany, does not expect to return daily, and daily return would be reasonable
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee answers the reasonableness question with 'yes'
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked whether they expect more than 60 work-related non-return days in the calendar year, answered 'yes' or 'no'; the answer is required when asked. The employee states their expectation for the year rather than proof as in the calculator; any proof goes to HR outside Lonio, with no upload. With 'no' to reasonableness the question is not asked

acceptance_criteria.title: Tariff without daily return
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Germany and does not expect to return daily
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio decides between cross-border and normal tariff
acceptance_criteria.then: if daily return is not reasonable, the normal tariff applies; if it is reasonable and more than 60 non-return days are expected, the normal tariff applies; if it is reasonable and no more than 60 non-return days are expected, the cross-border tariff applies (A becomes L, B becomes M, C becomes N, H becomes P). The result is always derived again from the latest answers. Cross-border results for tariffs A, B and H are part of the go-live comparison (see OQ-calculator-coverage)

stories.title: Liechtenstein: daily return and more than 45 non-return days
stories.i_want: every employee living in Liechtenstein to state first whether they expect to return daily to their main residence in Liechtenstein and, if not, whether they expect more than 45 work-related non-return days in the calendar year
stories.so_that: Lonio records, as the Zurich calculator does, either 'in principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement' or the normal tariff code with the double taxation agreement reservation, and flags the case for HR
stories.priority_reason: Liechtenstein residents work at Muster AG (F-hr_transcript-3f2c2a); Lonio now owns the tariff result (D-001) and must not ask needless tariff questions when there is in principle no liability (G-01).

acceptance_criteria.title: Liechtenstein residents are asked about daily return first
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's home address on the first working day is in Liechtenstein (so HR's rule makes them subject to source tax whatever their nationality)
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches the source tax questions
acceptance_criteria.then: before denomination, spouse and children questions, the employee is asked whether they expect to return daily to their main residence in Liechtenstein, answered 'yes' or 'no'; the answer is required. With 'no' they are then asked whether they expect more than 45 work-related non-return days in the calendar year, answered 'yes' or 'no' and required. The employee states their expectation for the year. Asking before the tariff questions is an assumption to be verified by a domain expert (D-040)

acceptance_criteria.title: In principle no source tax liability: tariff questions skipped
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Liechtenstein and either expects to return daily, or does not return daily and expects at most 45 non-return days
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio determines the source tax result
acceptance_criteria.then: Lonio records 'in principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement' instead of a tariff code, flags it for HR, and does not ask the denomination, spouse and children questions for source tax. How HR sees the flag is specified in the later HR-side spec (see OQ-hr-side-follow-ups). This follows the calculator; asking these residents at all is a decision to be verified by a domain expert (D-007)

examples.name: Calculator: no daily return, at most 45 days (zh_source_tax_calculator/F-zh_source_tax_calculator-fb87f1)

acceptance_criteria.title: More than 45 non-return days: normal tariff with DTA reservation
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Liechtenstein, does not expect to return daily and expects more than 45 non-return days
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio determines the source tax result
acceptance_criteria.then: the tariff questions (denomination, spouse, children) are asked, the normal tariff code is computed (never the cross-border tariff, which applies only to Germany residents) and recorded with the note 'subject to the double taxation agreement', flagged for HR. The result is always derived again from the latest answers. Recording the note and the flag is an assumption to be verified by a domain expert (D-040)
